topic: Under and over absorption of overheads
question: Explain the meaning of under-absorption and over-absorption of overheads. State their causes and how they are treated in cost accounts.
sources: Overheads: absorption of overheads using pre-determined rates and treatment of under/over absorbed overheads

points.label: Meaning
points.description: Overheads are absorbed using a pre-determined rate; if absorbed overheads are less than actual overheads it is under-absorption, and if more it is over-absorption.

points.label: Causes
points.description: Actual overhead expenses or actual activity (hours or output) differ from the estimates used to set the rate, for example due to idle capacity, seasonal changes or a change in methods.

points.label: Supplementary rate
points.description: Where the difference is large, a supplementary rate is used to adjust it over cost of sales, finished goods and work-in-progress.

points.label: Write off to costing P&L
points.description: Where the difference is small or due to abnormal reasons such as idle capacity or defective planning, it is written off to the costing profit and loss account.

points.label: Carry forward
points.description: Where the rate was set for a longer cycle (such as a seasonal business) the balance may be carried forward to the next period instead of being written off.
